messages.subject: Connecting to NCEP
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I have been following the Madison examples given, and receive an error when running the following line (after installing microclima) -

micro <- micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)

This is the error message -

There is a problem connecting to the NCEP database with the information provided. Try entering http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/psd/thredds/dodsC/Datasets/ncep.reanalysis2/gaussian_grid/air.2m.gauss.2016.nc.das into a web browser to obtain an error message.

I have searched for the error message which is as follows -

Error { code = 500; message = "net.openhft.chronicle.map.VanillaChronicleMap closed"; };

I have tried to figure out what this error message means but am coming up short as to what I need to do to fix it and progress.

Does anyone know how to fix this error? Apologies if it is in the forum already I have searched for the topic but can't find it.

Thank you,

Shane

These are the messages after running the code, before I get the prompt to search for the error message.
downloading DEM via package elevatr  Accessing raster elevation [=========================] 100% Mosaicing & Projecting Note: Elevation units are in meters. downloading weather data with package RNCEP via package microclima trying URL 'http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/psd/thredds/dodsC/Datasets/ncep.reanalysis2/gaussian_grid/air.2m.gauss.2016.nc.das' trying URL 'http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/psd/thredds/dodsC/Datasets/ncep.reanalysis2/gaussian_grid/air.2m.gauss.2016.nc.das' trying URL 'http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/psd/thredds/dodsC/Datasets/ncep.reanalysis2/gaussian_grid/air.2m.gauss.2016.nc.das' trying URL 'http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/psd/thredds/dodsC/Datasets/ncep.reanalysis2/gaussian_grid/air.2m.gauss.2016.nc.das' trying URL 'http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/psd/thredds/dodsC/Datasets/ncep.reanalysis2/gaussian_grid/air.2m.gauss.2016.nc.das' Error in NCEP.gather.gaussian(variable = variable, months.minmax = months.minmax, :

messages.subject: Re: era5 download issues
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dave,

Sorry for the late response! I asked the question and then went out of town for two conferences, so much so that I forgot I asked the question!

My input values for build_era5_request() was:
build_era5_request(xmin = -180, xmax = -175,
                            ymin = -90, ymax = 90,
                            start_time = "2022-01-01",
                            end_time = "2022-01-01",
                            outfile_name = "-180_-175")
Actually, I was trying to do this in a for loop and download the global era5 data for 2022 at intervals of 5 degrees of longitude (I have done so for the year 2019). I wonder if it is because I have downloaded too much era5 data with my account, so I am not allowed to continue to download data in batches.

Looking forward to your advice. Thank you very much for the help!

All the best,

Liang

> > > Hi André,
> > >
> > > If by model you mean the NicheMapR microclimate model, yes most of the NicheMapR wrapper functions that leverage the microclimate model have some option to save downloaded climate and re-access the local data, or you can modify one of the wrapper functions to access a custom climate dataset (from experience this may take a bit of effort). However I want to note that for all of the NicheMapR wrapper functions– including micro_era5 that uses mcera5– once you download the climate dataset once, if you set save = 1 then the climate forcing data will be saved (setting save = 2 will access saved climate data). messages.subject: Microclimate data for ectotherm
messages.body_plain:
Hi all！
I'm new to NicheMapR. I've encountered that the ectotherm function requires the utilization of a complete “micro” variable already stored in RAM. In a recent attempt to run ectotherm for a widely distributed lizard, I employed micro_terra to get hourly microclimate data for ectotherm. However, this resulted in the generation of excessively large "micro" variables. I am uncertain whether all the information contained in “micro” is essential for the proper execution of “ectotherm”. Is there a method to implement the “ectotherm” function in a manner similar to the “endo” function, wherein only specific data from the “micro” variables is provided, rather than the entirety of it?

messages.subject: Re: Microclimate data for ectotherm
messages.body_plain:
Yes - if you want to just calculate body temperature with no behaviour you could use the ectoR_devel function (see post on this within this discussion group by searching for "ectoR_devel - a modular version of the ectotherm model - now available"). Though it is slower because it's using all R code, no Fortran.

Alternatively, if you look into the default input arguments of the ectotherm function (type edit(ectotherm) in R to see this) you will see a number of items with micro$ (which I've pasted bellow). These are the ones it needs so you can just construct your own versions of those input arguments (they must have the same structure) or make a pared down micro list that only has those that the ectotherm model needs.
All the best,
Mike

  minshades = micro$minshade,
  maxshades = micro$maxshade,
   alpha_sub = (1 - micro$REFL),
   DEP = micro$DEP,
  KS = micro$KS[seq(1, 19, 2)],
  b = micro$BB[seq(1, 19, 2)],
  PE = micro$PE[seq(1, 19, 2)],
  metout = micro$metout,
  shadmet = micro$shadmet,
  soil = micro$soil,
  shadsoil = micro$shadsoil,
  soilmoist = micro$soilmoist,
  shadmoist = micro$shadmoist,
  humid = micro$humid,
  shadhumid = micro$shadhumid,
  soilpot = micro$soilpot,
  shadpot = micro$shadpot,
  tcond = micro$tcond,
  shadtcond = micro$shadtcond,
  rainfall = micro$RAINFALL,
  rainhr = rep(-1,nrow(metout)),
  preshr = rep(101325 * ((1 - (0.0065 * as.numeric(micro$elev) / 288)) ^ (1/0.190284)), nrow(metout)),
  elev = as.numeric(micro$elev),
  longitude = as.numeric(micro$longlat[1]),
  latitude = as.numeric(micro$longlat[2]),
